text:
mike: quick dump from today's regression run — noticed a cluster of OOMs on p3-large under mixed seq workloads. attaching profiling snippet.

mike: perf snapshot: 
```
Workspace peak: 24.6 GB
KV cache used: 9.2 GB (fragmented)
Temp allocs (attention kernel): 3.8 GB spike
Requests until OOM: 6
```

sophia: hmm, that attention kernel spike looks like the fused kernel path. when batch shapes are heterogeneous it allocs extra temp buffers.

anita: are those from compile-time kernel selection? we recently flipped auto-kernel for multihead-attn to heuristic-based.

mike: yep — change rolled in last friday. I ran a microbench vs previous. tail P95 latency up ~12% and memory tail worse.

kevin: could be workspace sizing + kernel choice tradeoff. fused kernel allocs per-batch scratch proportional to max-seq in batch; bad when big outliers.

sophia: proposed quick mitigation: force fallback kernel for batches where max_seq - median_seq > 128. keeps temp down, small perf hit.

anita: also seeing the KV cache fragmentation metric creep. allocator slabs not coalescing with frequent prefills + evictions.

mike: i ran a sim for eviction policy variants: LRU, size-aware LRU, and decode-weighted (weigh entries by downstream decode cost). results small sim (1M ops):

mike: sim output: 
```
LRU: avg cache hit 72%, tail latency 220ms
Size-aware LRU: hit 78%, tail 195ms
Decode-weighted: hit 80%, tail 170ms
```

kevin: decode-weighted wins but it increases bookkeeping overhead. we need fast approximate weights.

sophia: could use per-entry token_count + last_decode_time to estimate decode_cost ~ token_count * recent_decode_cpu_factor. maintain exponential avg.

anita: on allocator side i pushed a prototype for slab compaction: periodically scan small freed ranges and coalesce into larger free spans. bench shows fragmentation drop from 12%->3% on synthetic workload.

mike: nice. does compaction add latency spikes? background GC thread?

anita: background thread with throttled passes, stops when host load > 60%. no observable p99 impact in my test.

sophia: another lever: reduce per-request KV prefill cap from 64k to 16k tokens for hosted tier; forces more decode-on-demand but keeps cache from being poisoned by one huge request.

kevin: tradeoffs there: prefill saves decode work but hogs slab space. with compaction + decode-weighted eviction we can reclaim better.

perf-bot: bench run 1971239999-alloc-tune: after enabling compaction + decode-weighted eviction + kernel fallback: overall token throughput -3%, p95 latency -5%, OOMs 0 -> 0 (previously 3/day).

mike: that's promising. small throughput hit acceptable if OOMs disappear.

anita: one more micro-optimization: buffer reuse between decode and prefill phases. currently we alloc per-stage; reuse reduces transient peak by ~2.4 GB in our run.

sophia: can we adopt a staged allocator arena: primary workspace + aux cached buffers reused across requests for short-lived temp buffers?

kevin: yes — need to ensure per-request isolation for security, but reuse within request lifecycle is fine. put guard fence checks.

mike: action items:
- anita: land slab compaction prototype behind flag and perf gate (ETA 2 days)
- sophia: implement kernel fallback heuristic in runtime (ETA 1 day)
- kevin: wire decode-weighted eviction with approximate weights (ETA 3 days)
- mike: reduce default prefill cap for hosted -> set to 16k (trial) and monitor (ETA today)

sophia: I'll run a canary with 10% traffic after kernel fallback merged.

anita: i'll add metrics for fragmentation, compaction runs, and compaction CPU cost to console dashboards.

kevin: will add perf counters for eviction decisions (why an entry was evicted) so we can verify decode-weighted effect.

mike: thanks all. if anyone has a better sim harness for mixed seq shapes share it here.

sophia: pinging @mike for the perf traces link and @anita for compaction PR once ready. :thumbsup!
